## Purpose
Defines the `User` SQLAlchemy model — the account record every authenticated request resolves to, backing login, JWT validation, tier-based access, and the relationships to a user's chat sessions and workflow runs.

## Shape
- `User(Base)` — a single ORM class mapped to the `users` table.
- Identity/auth fields: `id` (UUID string PK), `email` (unique, indexed), `password_hash`, `password_changed_at`.
- Access-control fields: `tier` (default `"basic"`), `is_admin`, `preferred_model`.
- Bookkeeping: `created_at` / `updated_at` timestamps (UTC, auto-set/auto-updated).
- Relationships: `chat_sessions` and `workflow_runs`, both `back_populates` on the respective child models.

## Why this shape
`password_changed_at` exists specifically to support a cheap, enumeration-free "revoke all outstanding JWTs" pattern: any token issued (`iat`) before this timestamp is treated as revoked (implemented in `app/core/dependencies.py`), avoiding the need to track/blacklist individual tokens per password change.
